traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Restionaceae with Anarthriaceae, Centrolepidaceae, Ecdeiocoleaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves alternate; leaves simple; veins parallel; leaves evergreen or deciduous; stipules present or absent; leaf rosettes basal or none; plants usually dioecious, sometimes hermaphrodite, monoecious or polygamous; ovary superior; stems herbaceous; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth tepals or absent; fruit capsule or nut, sometimes follicle; stamens (1-) 2 to 3; carpels (1-) 3. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 265, 268, 269, family Restionaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral; read as "spiral".

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 265, 268, 269, family Restionaceae: inflorescence solitary or branched groups of spikelets; read as "solitary".

traits.life_span.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 265, 268, 269, family Restionaceae: life span perennial; read as "perennial".

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 265, 268, 269, family Restionaceae: rhizome habit short_creeping (rhizomatous or stoloniferous), usually; read as {"short_creeping": "usually"}.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Restionaceae, with the parts of Restionaceae it codes as families of their own (Anarthriaceae), whose further states read as sometimes: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a rhizome; with them, usually a rhizome. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add achene (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 265, 268, 269: achene, nut or capsule.
